rules: Pick the first task, in file order, whose status is todo and whose depends_on tasks all pass.
Skip tasks with human set to true unless the owner is taking part; set them to blocked and state in evidence what the owner must decide or check.
Set status to in_progress and owner to your agent name before starting.
Change only status, owner, passes, and evidence fields.
One task is one pull request, and the pull request marks the task done in this file.
Set passes to true only after every acceptance item is verified.
Put the verification command output summary in evidence.

Never edit, remove, or weaken acceptance items outside a Product Owner pass. The Product Owner approves a scope-only edit and logs its reason; an edit that changes on-screen wording, look or product direction needs an owner approval file. The owner can veto any of it.
Write the failing tests for a task's acceptance items before implementing, and never edit those tests while implementing.

A playback task is one whose change makes the app send a media, playlist, segment, subtitle, trickplay or artwork request, or a playstate report. It passes only when its wire test passes against Jellyscale: the Authorization header on every request, no token in any URL, no redirect followed, no other origin contacted.

A task whose title names a Jellyscale issue waits for that issue: set it to blocked with the issue's state in evidence. Nothing may depend on such a task, and the release does not wait for it. Never work around a missing server feature with a token in a URL.
Set status to blocked and explain in evidence when a dependency, an owner decision, or a Shield check is missing.
Use the model and skill named on the task.
Tasks with human set to true need the owner: a decision on look, wording or direction, or a check on the Nvidia Shield. The acceptance names it.
The Product Owner (Fable 5.2) owns the backlog and the priorities: only a Product Owner pass adds, splits, reorders or drops tasks, after triaging tasks/backlog.jsonl. The owner can veto any of it.
Append deferred or newly found work to the backlog, tasks/backlog.jsonl; any agent or pull request may.

Before adopting any dependency, verify from primary sources that it is actively maintained: recent releases and commits, not archived, and no maintainer statement of maintenance mode or supersession. Record the check in the task's spec, and re-check every dependency when a phase starts.
There is no done.json. The desktop app's task list lives only in the tag desktop-tauri-final.
Never commit a server address, a credential, or the owner's name.
Read tasks through `pnpm task` (next, show, list, set); never load tasks/prd.json whole. Keep evidence to 600 characters naming the PR or commit.

The UTF-8 check runs in every decoding round, so /Items/%25c0%25ae%25c0%25ae/x is refused, and a path that still holds a percent-escape after the last round is refused, so five rounds of encoding (%252525252e) are refused
The one client applies the same additions to the encoded path of every session and closing call (C2), shown by a test through the client's call factory

tasks.title: T3 hardening: close the review lows of T3-24, T3-25, T3-28, T3-29 and T3-30
acceptance: The spec lists every finding of the five reviews (plans 011-t3-24, 012-t3-25, 012-t3-28, 013-t3-29 and 011-t3-30 under docs/plans/active, and the backlog lines this task took) with whether it still holds on main; one already fixed is closed with the commit, and the rest are closed by the items below

The request path rule, in RequestPath.kt and request-path.ts alike, refuses a segment that is only dots once the characters UTS #46 ignores (U+00AD and the variation selectors among them) or trailing spaces are removed, and refuses the characters a proxy may fold to a separator or a ; (U+FF0F, U+FF3C, U+FF1B, U+FE54, U+037E), as written or after any decoding round; a server address whose base path fails the rule is refused before any session opens; the spec rules on whether a query pair needs a rule for a ; or a control character and records why

New tests in files no manifest freezes: a closing call sent through the client the logout uses is refused outside the base path; RequestPath.isSafe refuses the raw C1 controls and the raw dot-like characters; a 100,000-deep object through the one client is unexpected-response

The native signIn closes the session when anything fails after SessionRegistry.open; the OutOfMemoryError mapping allocates nothing after the catch, or docs/security.md and decision 0005 state the limit; the number of values in a native answer is bounded, with the bound taken from the largest recorded answer; the reference transport and the TV adapter refuse an answer nested deeper than 64, or the spec shows from a test under Hermes and Node why they need not

The ELF reader records a problem for a REL or RELA section not linked to .dynsym, so L0 fails closed, and for an SHT_REL section or tests that path; a test shows L0 for a library with an undefined dispatcher symbol and packed relocations

D8's reader (scripts/octave-module-packages.mjs) reads a whole qualified package name and fails on a segment that is not a plain identifier, strips comments in one left-to-right pass, and fails closed on a Gradle namespace it cannot read, each with a test; a test asserts the text "D8 read no Octave Kotlin or Java source"

The dex check reports an entry whose CRC-32 does not match as damage in one ERROR tv apk dex: line, and counts a sink site once when the superclass walk finds it again; the source scan (pnpm lint:network) exempts only client sockets in DirectSocketFactory.kt and names the listening, datagram, factory, provider, MediaExtractor and MediaMetadataRetriever openers; the spec rules on a K4 twin for android.net.Network's opens and android.net.http

scripts/check-adb-output.mjs gives a finding for a template-literal specifier, a re-exporting helper, an interpreter given as a literal program, and a shell option under a quoted key or in a variable, each with a test, or docs/security.md lists the one the spec shows cannot be read as not covered

docs/security.md and ARCHITECTURE.md say what is built and no more: a stack overflow or out-of-memory error is never network; the debugOptimized run was the judge on a recorded cut; the inspector check also reads one debugger-only string; D8 covers what it reads; D0's bounds claim covers dex entries; and the decision 0005 bullet gives the path rule as built. The PR calls out every changed security rule

No frozen file changes: where a frozen test contradicts an item the task returns to the Product Owner. pnpm tv:apk:check still passes on the release APK the tv CI job builds, and the PR quotes its lines
